title: Official integrations README labels SDK 0.2.0 as current while npm latest is 0.7.0

environment.integration: public CALL-E integrations README and npm registry metadata

preconditions: npm CLI or direct access to the public npm registry
steps: Open https://github.com/CALLE-AI/call-e-integrations and locate the SDK section.
Observe the Current server SDK packages label for @call-e/calle@0.2.0.
Run npm view @call-e/calle version engines dist-tags --json.
Compare the documented current version with the latest registry version.
expected: A package explicitly labeled current in the official setup README matches the registry's latest stable release, or the documentation explains why it intentionally points to an older release.
actual: The README identifies @call-e/calle@0.2.0 as current, while the npm registry returned latest version 0.7.0 on 2026-09-11.
impact: A developer following the unpinned install command receives 0.7.0 while the adjacent version statement sets expectations for 0.2.0. This makes setup reports and API-surface troubleshooting harder to compare.
suggested_change: Generate the displayed version from release metadata, replace the hard-coded version with a latest-stable link, or state that the number is an intentionally tested baseline rather than the current package version.
limitations: This finding concerns public version metadata only.
No SDK method or authenticated CALL-E API behavior was tested.
Registry metadata can change after the recorded timestamp.
